findings.reason: the map is what the coordinator dispatches from, and an unordered pair of writers on `reckon/serve.py` and `reckon/metadata_index.py` produces the merge collision this plan's earlier wiring finding on `s49`/`s31` was raised and fixed for.
findings.text: the dependency map lists `s31: [s46, s50]` and nothing else, but §31's write paths are `reckon/metadata_index.py` and `reckon/serve.py`, which §51 (serve.py) and §52 (serve.py, metadata_index.py) also write and which have no ordering against §31; §52's own text orders it "after §50 and §51, which write the same modules" and never mentions §31, so a coordinator obeying the map can dispatch §31 and §52 into the same two files at once

findings.reason: a node implementing the stated control would log a negative control that runs red for no reason or is quietly abandoned, leaving the first half of the deliverable with no guard at all; the second half (the file-open count) is the only half this node's gate would really prove.
findings.text: the first done-when item ("the index's figure row and `figure_rows`' row for the same path agree on every shared key") is satisfied by construction once the index reads through `figure_rows`, and the declared control ("rename one output key of `figure_rows`, and the agreement case fails") cannot break it: the same rename reaches both rows, and the key comparison is over the intersection of keys, which simply shrinks; the control the change actually needs is one that restores the duplicate derivation (keep `metadata_index._figure_row`), where the index row then carries the old key set and the case fails

findings.reason: this is the mechanism the section was written for (replacing §49's per-process watch), and if the counter is not shared the fix works in a one-process test and fails in the served deployment the plan exists to fix; the plan must say the counter is persisted on the same node-local storage and read on every call, and the done-when must add an arm where process A writes and a fresh process B's next call recomputes.
findings.text: "A write counter that the store's single plan writer, `reckon/_store.py`'s `write_plan`, advances after every write … so an uncommitted plan write is seen at once by every process": the snapshot is persisted on node-local storage shared by every process on the node, but the counter is described as owned in an existing module with no statement that it is persisted and re-read per call, and a module-level counter is process-local; the whole point of the persisted snapshot is that a second process — the current-code child, a restarted MCP server, the HTTP server — answers its first call from the file, so a write made by one process leaves the others' keys unmoved and they serve a stale composed roadmap for up to the 120 s window; the done-when does not close this either: "a fresh process with nothing changed answers its first call from the persisted snapshot" exercises no cross-process write at all
